paths.title: Python Data Model and Collections
paths.description: Use mutability, identity, iteration, and collection semantics deliberately.
concept: Python assignment binds a name to an object; it does not automatically copy that object.
This distinction explains aliasing, mutation, default-argument pitfalls, and why two names can observe the same list.
workflow: Choose a collection intentionally
Match the data structure to ordering, uniqueness, lookup, and mutation needs.
Clear collection choices make code simpler.
Use a list for ordered mutable items.
Use a tuple for fixed records.
Use a set for uniqueness and membership tests.
Use a dictionary for key-to-value lookup.
Use comprehensions for readable transformations.
Copy explicitly when independent mutation is required.
question: Recognize aliasing
After b = a where a is a list, what happens when b.append(3) runs?
Only b changes
Only a changes
Both names observe the appended item
Python raises automatically
Both names refer to the same mutable list until an explicit copy or rebinding occurs.
checklist: Collection correctness review
Check that collection behavior matches the domain.
Bugs often come from accidental order, shared mutation, or ambiguous missing values.
The chosen type matches ordering requirements.
Mutation is intentional.
Copies are explicit where ownership changes.
Dictionary missing-key behavior is defined.
Set use does not discard needed duplicates.
Iteration does not modify the same collection unsafely.

paths.title: Functions, Errors, and Resource Safety
paths.description: Design clear function contracts and handle failures without hiding defects.
concept: A useful function defines accepted inputs, returned values, side effects, and expected exceptions.
Broad exception handling makes programming errors and anticipated operational failures indistinguishable.
workflow: Handle an operation safely
Validate assumptions and release resources even when work fails.
Context managers and narrow exception handling keep cleanup reliable.
Validate caller-controlled inputs.
Open resources with a context manager.
Catch only exceptions you can resolve or translate.
Preserve the original cause when raising a new error.
Log actionable context without secrets.
Let unexpected defects propagate to tests or monitoring.
question: Choose the narrow handler
Which approach is safest when converting user text to an integer?
Catch every exception in the program
Catch ValueError around the conversion
Ignore all failures
Use a bare except and return zero
ValueError is the expected conversion failure; narrower handling avoids hiding unrelated defects.
checklist: Function design review
Make functions predictable and testable.
Small, explicit contracts reduce coupling and simplify failure tests.
Inputs and outputs have clear meanings.
Mutable default arguments are avoided.
Side effects are limited or documented.
Exceptions preserve useful context.
Resources close on every path.
Pure logic is separated from I/O.
Boundary cases have tests.

paths.title: Testing and Packaging Python Code
paths.description: Structure modules, isolate dependencies, and ship repeatable Python programs.
concept: A package is an explicit dependency boundary
Modules and packages organize reusable code and make imports, tests, and distribution predictable.
A project should separate application code, tests, configuration, and generated artifacts.
workflow: Create a reliable Python project
Make installation and testing reproducible from a clean environment.
The project should not require hidden global packages or manual file placement.
Place importable code in a package directory.
Declare runtime and development dependencies.
Use an isolated virtual environment.
Write tests against public behavior.
Run tests from the project root.
Build the package or application artifact.
Install and smoke-test the built artifact.
question: Patch the correct dependency
In a unit test, where should a dependency normally be patched?
Where it is looked up by the code under test
Only in the dependency's original package
In every module in the project
Nowhere; tests cannot isolate dependencies
Patching the name used by the module under test replaces the actual lookup performed during the test.
checklist: Python release checklist
Confirm that users receive the behavior that tests covered.
A green source test run is not enough if packaging omits modules or data.
Dependencies are declared appropriately.
Tests pass in a clean environment.
Static checks run on all modules.
The build contains required package data.
Entry points start correctly.
Configuration is externalized.
The built artifact is installed and smoke-tested.
